result.summary: Read docs/agents/design/REQ-025.md and docs/agents/design/REQ-025-schema.md in full, then read apps/bot/src/domain/notification.ts, scheduler/rateLimiter.ts, scheduler/runner.ts line by line against both design docs, plus the full withdraw.ts/index.ts/user.ts/schema.ts diffs. Every element matches the design precisely: the ordered rule table in REQ-025.md §3.1 is implemented step-for-step (unconditional blocked check before the classification branch, marketing-only broadcastOptIn read, the single atomic ledger INSERT before the send, the ledger row never rolled back on send failure), the schema doc's table shape (text kind, UNIQUE(registration_id, kind), restrict-everywhere FK, DEFAULT now() timestamps) matches schema.ts and the generated migration 0005_violet_venom.sql statement-for-statement, and withdraw.ts's rewrite matches REQ-025.md §4 exactly (ctx removed, sender injected, promotedRegistrationId sourced from outcome.promotion.registrationId, thin composeMessage closure, index.ts wiring the one process-wide sender/scheduler). pgErrorCode() unwrap fix VERIFIED AGAINST THE ACTUAL DRIZZLE-ORM SOURCE, not trusted from the report: read node_modules/drizzle-orm/errors.d.ts directly -- DrizzleQueryError's constructor signature is `(query, params, cause?: Error)`, i.e. the underlying pg driver error (carrying `.code`) is genuinely nested one level down on `.cause`, confirming the fix's premise is correct, not just plausible. The helper's fallback (top-level `.code` first, then `.cause.code`) is the right shape for this library version (drizzle-orm 0.45.2, exact-pinned). INDEPENDENTLY RE-VERIFIED AC1 MYSELF, constructed fresh (not BACKEND-DEV's script): wrote my own throwaway seed script and a child script under apps/bot/.reviewer-scratch/ (deleted after use), seeded a fresh chapter/user/venue/event/admitted-registration via drizzle directly against the already-running scratch Postgres (bot-postgres-1, port 55432, freshly re-migrated by me via `npx drizzle-kit migrate` to confirm the 0005 migration applies cleanly). Ran the child script as two GENUINELY SEPARATE `npx tsx` OS process invocations (not two in-process calls) against the same (registrationId, userId): process 1 called sendLedgeredNotification(kind:'reminder_24h') with a sender stub that resolves (simulating a successful Telegram delivery), appended a SENT marker to a file, then called `process.exit(0)` immediately -- placing the simulated kill exactly where REQ-025.md §3.2 says AC1's 'exactly one' wording is provable (after sender.send(...) has resolved, not mid-flight). Process 2, a wholly fresh process with no shared memory, re-ran the identical call: got `{kind:'skipped-already-sent'}`, appended a NOT-SENT marker. Marker file contents: exactly one 'SENT' line, one 'NOT-SENT:skipped-already-sent' line. Queried notification_ledger directly afterward: exactly one row for that (registration_id, kind). Confirms exactly one message delivered across a genuine two-process restart, independently reproduced. INDEPENDENTLY RE-VERIFIED AC2 MYSELF: `grep -rn "new Set|new Map|WeakMap" src/domain/notification.ts src/scheduler/*.ts src/handlers/withdraw.ts` -> no match, confirming no in-memory idempotency tracker anywhere in this design's own files. Direct duplicate INSERT via my own raw-SQL script against the same ledger row from the AC1 test -> `error.code === '23505'`, `constraint: 'uq_notification_ledger_registration_kind'` -- the DB UNIQUE constraint alone is the mechanism. INDEPENDENTLY RE-VERIFIED AC3/AC4 MYSELF with my own fixtures (distinct from BACKEND-DEV's), against sendLedgeredNotification directly: a broadcast_opt_in=false, non-blocked user got `{kind:'sent'}` for a transactional call and `{kind:'skipped-no-broadcast-opt-in'}` for a marketing call on the same user, one delivery total -- AC3. A blocked=true, broadcast_opt_in=true user got `{kind:'skipped-blocked'}` for BOTH a transactional and a marketing call, zero deliveries -- AC4. AC5 confirmed by direct read: SendNotificationInput.classification: SendClassification has no `?` and no default value anywhere in domain/notification.ts. INDEPENDENTLY RE-VERIFIED AC6 MYSELF with my own stub (not BACKEND-DEV's script): a fake grammy Bot whose api.sendMessage throws a real `GrammyError` (constructed with the library's own actual constructor shape, error_code 429, parameters.retry_after=1) on the first call and succeeds on the second. `createRateLimitedSender(...).send(...)` resolved after exactly 2 underlying calls, elapsed ~1005ms (honoring the stubbed retry_after over initialBackoffMs), single logical send resolved exactly once. REQ-023 REGRESSION CHECK on the now-migrated withdraw.ts path: re-ran the EXISTING (not new) withdraw.test.ts suite in isolation with --reporter=verbose and confirmed by name that 'REQ-023 AC6: the promoted person is notified even with broadcast_opt_in=false' and 'S10 rework: a blocked promoted person's promotion completes with no notification sent' both ran (dbAvailable, not skipped) and PASSED, exercising the real grammY dispatch through makeWithdrawConfirmCallbackHandler -> sendPromotionNotification -> sendLedgeredNotification end-to-end against real Postgres. Read both test bodies to confirm they genuinely exercise the migrated path (broadcastOptIn/blocked set via direct DB update, dispatched via bot.handleUpdate(), asserting on captured sendMessage payloads) rather than being stale pre-migration assertions. Confirms REQ-023's promotion notification behavior (AC6, AC8-equivalent S10 case) is intact post-migration. scheduler/runner.ts overlap guard and failure isolation: read the code (per-job `running` boolean set/cleared around job.run(), a rejected promise caught in `.catch()` and logged, never rethrown, `.finally()` always clears the flag) -- correct by inspection. INDEPENDENTLY CONSTRUCTED A TEST to confirm, not just read: three jobs -- a 200ms-duration job ticking every 30ms, a job that throws every tick, and an independent fast job ticking every 20ms -- run together for 500ms via startScheduledJobs. Result: the slow job ran only 3 times with max observed concurrency 1 (the overlap guard correctly skipped the ~13 ticks that fired while its previous run was still in flight, never running two copies concurrently); the throwing job's failure was caught and logged 9 times without an uncaught rejection or process crash; the independent fast job ran 17 times, unaffected by either the slow job's duration or the throwing job's repeated failures. Confirms both properties genuinely hold, not just by design intent. MINOR issue 1 (pgErrorCode .cause unwrap): ACCEPTED AS IMPLEMENTED. Verified correct against the actual library source (see above) -- this is a real, correctly-diagnosed and correctly-fixed bug, not a design deviation. No rework needed. MINOR issue 2 (runner.ts's internal logger instead of a threaded log-level parameter): ACCEPTED AS IMPLEMENTED for this run. The design's own stated signature (`startScheduledJobs(jobs)`, one parameter) genuinely conflicts with its rule-table's logging clause naming 'this codebase's existing log.ts logger' with no parameter to carry it -- BACKEND-DEV's literal reading of the signature over the prose is a reasonable resolution of that internal design ambiguity, correctly disclosed rather than silently resolved, and has zero behavioral effect today since no job ships in this requirement (`startScheduledJobs([])`) and log.ts's own LEVEL_ORDER makes `.error()` always fire regardless of the threshold passed to createLogger -- verified this claim by reading log.ts directly (LEVEL_ORDER.error = 3, the max value; a `.error()` call is never gated). Judgment: no design/rework follow-up needed now; correctly deferred to REQ-026/027 (the first requirements to actually populate the job list) if a threaded configured-log-level ever becomes behaviorally relevant. Domain logic outside handler bodies (decisions/0004): confirmed. withdraw.ts's sendPromotionNotification is a thin composeMessage closure (i18n/formatting only) plus one call to sendLedgeredNotification; makeWithdrawConfirmCallbackHandler's only change is threading the sender parameter through and reading outcome.promotion.registrationId (already-existing data, no new logic). All admission/blocked/broadcastOptIn/idempotency rules live in domain/notification.ts, which has no grammy import (grepped: none). scheduler/rateLimiter.ts is the one deliberate exception the design itself names (the concrete NotificationSender implementation, which necessarily imports grammy to wrap Bot['api']) -- not a domain-logic leak, since it contains no admission/consent/idempotency business rule, only HTTP-retry/pacing mechanics. No `now()` in a time-dependent predicate: notification_ledger's created_at/updated_at are DEFAULT now() write-time facts, never read back into any predicate anywhere in this diff (grepped domain/notification.ts, rateLimiter.ts, runner.ts, withdraw.ts for any read of notificationLedger.createdAt: none) -- correctly falls under decisions/0006's audit/bookkeeping-default carve-out, not the time-dependent-query rule. No decisions/0006 violation. Migration reviewed as SQL directly (decisions/0005): apps/bot/drizzle/0005_violet_venom.sql is exactly one CREATE TABLE (purely additive, no existing table altered, no personal-data column touched), one FK ALTER with ON DELETE RESTRICT, one CREATE UNIQUE INDEX -- matches the schema design's own predicted SQL statement-for-statement. No PII column dropped or rewritten, so no SECURITY-REVIEWER migration sign-off is triggered by S13's own rule -- S9/S10 remain the substantive review surface for Step 2c, which is exactly what this requirement is about. Workspace/build-output check: no new npm workspace, no apps/* rename, no build-output directory moved -- confirmed via `git diff master...HEAD --stat` (only existing apps/bot/src, apps/bot/drizzle, docs, handoffs files changed). No scratch docker build required per this role's trigger condition. COMMANDS RE-RUN MYSELF, REAL OUTPUT (repo root, scratch Postgres bot-postgres-1 already running, re-migrated by me): `npm run lint` -> exit 0, 0 errors (2 pre-existing unrelated apps/web LCP warnings only, unchanged by this diff). `npm run build` -> exit 0, both workspaces clean (Next.js build succeeded; apps/bot's tsc clean). `TEST_DATABASE_URL=postgres://bot:bot@localhost:55432/bot npx vitest run --no-file-parallelism` (repo root) -> 19 files / 217 tests passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped -- matches BACKEND-DEV's reported count exactly, independently re-run by me. Scope check: `git diff master...HEAD --stat` touches exactly the design's own file list (schema.ts, the new domain/notification.ts + scheduler/{rateLimiter,runner}.ts, domain/user.ts, handlers/withdraw.ts + its test, handlers/my.test.ts, index.ts, the drizzle migration + meta files) plus docs/agents/design/*, this run's own handoffs. No scope creep. All my own scratch verification files (apps/bot/.reviewer-scratch/, .reviewer-scratch2/) were deleted immediately after use -- `git status --short` confirmed clean before this commit.

result.next_action: Route to SECURITY-REVIEWER (Step 2c) -- mandatory, S9 (restart-idempotency) and S10 (transactional-vs-marketing, blocked-skips-both) are central to this requirement's own stated purpose. My own assessment: the idempotency mechanism is a real DB UNIQUE constraint (independently re-verified via direct duplicate insert and a genuine two-process kill/restart), the blocked/broadcastOptIn branching is independently re-verified against fresh fixtures, and the withdraw.ts migration does not regress REQ-023's existing AC6/S10 behavior. SECURITY-REVIEWER should still independently confirm rather than take this as sufficient, per this pipeline's re-derive rule -- with particular attention to whether the accepted 'under-sending on crash' risk (REQ-025.md §3.2, a deliberate design tradeoff favoring under- over over-sending) and the two MINOR implementation issues (pgErrorCode's .cause unwrap, runner.ts's internal-vs-threaded logger) warrant any note in their own sign-off, though neither blocks this review's PASS.
